subject: Ephemeral capacity credit, rate-fallback path, and final discount handoff
messages:
From: Anna Park <anna@quickcommerce.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@quickcommerce.com
Date: 2026-11-01T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Immediate need: launch week headroom + pricing ask

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. LaunchWeek (Nov 15-22) looks like it will double our peak QPS vs the load you saw in the POC. We need a short-term plan so our product team doesn't hit hard throttles.

Two asks:
- Can Redwood provide a temporary throughput uplift (approx +3x burst capacity) for the launch window and how would that be billed? We expect it to be a 7‑day window.
- Can we get a one‑time discount on the overrun true‑up if we commit to a 12‑month reserved pool afterwards?

If helpful, procurement is copied — happy to jump on a quick call.

Best,
Anna Park
Head of Platform, QuickCommerce

[attachment: TrafficForecast_QC_NovLaunch.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@quickcommerce.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate need: launch week headroom + pricing ask

Anna —

Appreciate the heads up and the traffic file. Short answer: yes, we can support a temporary +3x headroom and we have two common paths to minimize sticker shock:

1) Ephemeral uplift (pay-as-you-go) — instant capacity increase charged at standard on-demand rates; any overrun is invoiced on the following invoice.

2) Short-window reservation (7‑day provisional commit) — you prepay a discounted slab for that 7‑day window; we apply any overrun beyond the slab at a reduced overrun rate. If you convert to a 12‑month reserved commitment within 30 days, we credit X% of the provisional slab back (applied to the first invoice of the contract).

From a discount standpoint Ben and I can propose a blended overrun cap if you pick option 2. We've attached a provisional workbook with the blended math.

Quick questions before I price final:
- Confirm that the +3x applies to sustained QPS for the 7 days (not sustained 30-day).
- Any hard SLOs for tail latency during the window? Our recommended safety band assumes up to 250ms p95.

I can do a 30‑minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the invoice flow.

—Michael
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

[attachment: QC_Burst_Proposal_v3.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Park <anna@quickcommerce.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate need: launch week headroom + pricing ask

Anna —

Poking at the numbers in Michael's sheet. If QuickCommerce takes the provisional 7‑day slab (option 2), we can do:
- 18% discount on the provisional slab vs on‑demand for that 7‑day window
- Overrun rate capped at 1.6x the on‑demand rate (instead of 2.2x) for any usage above the slab during that window
- If you convert to a 12‑month reserved commit within 30 days, we will apply a credit equal to 40% of what you paid for the provisional slab toward the first month's reserved invoice (credit cannot exceed $50k).

Edge cases to call out so procurement is clear:
- Metering granularity is per-minute; throttles will still apply if sustained concurrency exceeds hardware limits — the provisional slab guarantees aggregate throughput but not per-instance tail isolation.
- We need a PO or an approved SOW for the provisional slab to stand up capacity (we can fast-track provisioning once PO is approved).

If you'd like, I'll draft a short SOW appendix and a line-item quote for procurement.

Thanks,
Ben
Sr. Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Anna Park <anna@quickcommerce.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: QuickCommerce Procurement <procurement@quickcommerce.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Immediate need: launch week headroom + pricing ask

Thanks Michael/Ben — this is helpful and closer to what we were hoping for. Procurement confirmed they can issue a PO this week if we have a short SOW and the provisional numbers. A couple of follow-ups so we can move fast:

1) Please send the SOW appendix (7‑day provisional slab + overrun cap language) — procurement wants explicit billing examples.
2) Can you include a fallback policy: if the provisional slab can't be provisioned in time, we want an automatic downgrade to on‑demand with a 24‑hour notice and a pro‑rated credit for missed capacity.
3) On the 40% conversion credit: can you confirm whether it applies before or after taxes and whether it affects committed volume tiers once moved to reserved?

If you can get the SOW and the sample invoice by EOD tomorrow we can route the PO and lock the provisional window.

Best,
Anna
Head of Platform, QuickCommerce
